backtracking.reason: Phase 3.1 matched coarse silhouettes but used a solid collar, heavy shoulders, cylindrical prongs, and a smooth gemstone proxy that did not resemble the reference setting.

accepted_improvements: solid cylindrical seat replaced by two separated gallery rails
four slender cathedral shoulder struts replace heavy wedges
open under-stone negative space is represented
four prongs taper inward and include separate tip beads
gemstone uses polygonal crown and pavilion facets instead of a smooth dome
shank thickness reduced to better match the reference
metal remains one solid and gemstone remains one separate solid
STEP, STL, OBJ, and GLB exports contain the complete hoop and head
remaining_differences: side/back head width remains narrower than the reference
prongs are straight tapered members rather than curved claw profiles
gallery rail and basket-strut positions need image-fitted adjustment
front shoulder silhouette remains more triangular than the reference
angled camera and asymmetric shoulder fit remain the weakest view
sixteen-sided gemstone is a faceted proxy, not a full round-brilliant facet arrangement
dimensions remain provisional until one physical measurement is supplied
conclusion: Phase 3.2 is a genuine structural improvement over Phase 3.1 even though the deliberately open/slender topology gives a lower filled-silhouette IoU than the overfilled Phase 3.1 proxy. It is the correct baseline for the next local fitting loop, but it is not final manufacturing CAD.
